question.problem: Estimate $\sqrt{3.9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.5)$ using a differential $\text{d}f$ of the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ at the point $(4,\frac{\pi }{2}).$ Round your answer to $3$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}x+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡y}{2\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x-\sqrt{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

At the point $(4,\frac{\pi }{2}),$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y) & =\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})}{2\sqrt{4}}\,\text{d}x-\sqrt{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})\,\text{d}y \\  & =0\,\text{d}x-2\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

So, if we move to the point $(4+Δx,\frac{\pi }{2}+Δy),$ then we can approximate the change in $f$ as

$$
Δf≈0\,Δx-2\,Δy
$$

Note that 

$$
\sqrt{3.9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.5)=f(3.9,1.5),
$$

so we want to move to the point $(3.9,1.5).$

Moving from $(4,\frac{\pi }{2})$ to $(3.9,1.5),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δx & =3.9-4=-0.1, \\ Δy & =1.5-\frac{\pi }{2}≈-0.070796.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δf & ≈0\cdot (-0.1)-2(-0.070796) \\  & ≈0+0.141592 \\  & ≈0.141592.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that the value of $f$ increases by about $0.141592.$ Consequently, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3.9,1.5) & ≈f(4,\frac{\pi }{2})+0.141592 \\ \sqrt{3.9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(1.5) & ≈\sqrt{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+0.141592 \\  & ≈0+0.141592 \\  & ≈0.142,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
